tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.take: The Thursday night appetizer is two teams going nowhere — Temple 2-8, Rice 1-9 — but the number has already told a story: it opened Temple -4 and is down to -2.5, with the total climbing from 47.5 to 51.5. Both teams are on a short week with four days of rest, and Rice flew 1,340 miles east. Our fair number makes Temple a narrow 51.9% favorite on the spread, and ESPN Bet is still hanging -2.5 at -105, ten cents off the -115 market — that's the board edge, a price edge rather than a matchup call. The weather is a non-factor: clear skies, about 51°F at kickoff, wind 5 mph.
games.title: Rice at Temple: the number moved, the price didn't
games.verdict: LEAN: Temple -2.5 — a board edge at -105; the price is 10 cents off the market.
games.weather: Outdoor; clear, ~51°F at kickoff, wind 5 mph, rain 0-3%. No NWS alerts.

games.take: Thursday Night Football is a 3-7 team against a 3-6 team, and yet Houston is laying 12.5 — because Indianapolis lost most of its offensive line and secondary to the injury report. Both starting tackles (Raimann, Travis) are out, corner Charvarius Ward is out, and the Colts sold off Buckner, Nelson, Allen and Downs at the deadline. Houston has its own absences — Danielle Hunter, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Woody Marks are all out — but David Montgomery is back healthy. The line opened around -10 and is now -12.5 nearly everywhere, so the value has already been taken; our fair number makes Houston an 86.6% favorite to win, and no price on the side clears our 0.75% bar. No true edge, but the lean is Houston -12.5: the Colts' roster tonight looks nothing like the one that won in September.
games.title: Colts at Texans: a 12.5-point favorite with a 3-6 record
games.verdict: LEAN: HOU -12.5 — no true edge on the side; the Colts are down both starting tackles after a deadline sell-off.
games.weather: Indoor (NRG Stadium roof); 68°F, 0% rain outside. No weather factor.

games.take: Golden State closes a five-game trip in Memphis running on fumes: Curry is out with an oblique tear, Butler is out with an ACL injury, Moody is out, and Draymond Green is expected to sit for rest. The Warriors have dropped four straight since Curry went down, losing by 7, 38, 21 and 22 points. Memphis is 11-4 and 11-4 against the spread, though the Grizzlies have their own absences — Ty Jerome, Scotty Pippen Jr. and GG Jackson are out. Our fair number makes Memphis a 51.2% favorite on the spread, and ESPN Bet is still hanging -6.5 at even money while the market sits at -6.5 -110 and -7.5 elsewhere. That's the board edge.
games.title: Warriors at Grizzlies: Golden State's injury list meets a hot Memphis side
games.verdict: LEAN: MEM -6.5 — a board edge at +100; the price is the story, not the matchup.

games.take: San Antonio is 12-3 and coming off a 12-game winning streak snapped Tuesday by Detroit, with Wembanyama averaging 28.4 points and 12 rebounds. The Clippers are 4-9 and missing Bradley Beal, Brandon Ingram and Jordan Miller. The spread opened at -16.5 and has come down to -15.5 — still a huge number, and our fair number makes San Antonio an 89.9% favorite to win outright, but no price on the side or the spread clears our 0.75% bar. No true edge, but the lean is San Antonio -15.5: Wemby at home against a short-handed 4-9 team, with the caveat that 15.5 points is a lot to lay and the model gap says the number is closer than the record suggests.
games.title: Clippers at Spurs: Wemby and a 15.5-point number
games.venue: Frost Bank Center, San Antonio, TX
games.verdict: LEAN: SAS -15.5 — no true edge on the side; the Spurs at home, whole at the top, against a short-handed Clippers side.

games.our_fair: Trail Blazers 79.9% / Bucks 20.1% (devigged Pinnacle fair, moneyline)
games.take: Milwaukee is 1-14, has lost 11 straight, and is on the second night of a back-to-back after playing in Miami on Wednesday — the worst start in franchise history. Portland is 9-5 and rested, but the Blazers are short too: Ja Morant and Shaedon Sharpe are out, and Deni Avdija (24.2 points a game) is questionable with a foot problem. Our fair number makes Portland a 79.9% favorite to win, and no price on the side clears our 0.75% bar. No true edge, but the lean is Portland -10.5: a rested team against a tired one on an 11-game skid — with the warning that the Blazers' own injury list is why this number is 10.5 and not 13.
games.title: Trail Blazers at Bucks: a 1-14 team on a back-to-back
games.verdict: LEAN: POR -10.5 — no true edge on the side; the rested 9-5 team against a 1-14 team on night two of a back-to-back.

games.take: The night's best game is a coin flip with a low total. Minnesota is 11-4 and 7-2 at home, and 8-3 since Anthony Edwards went down with a knee injury — LaMelo Ball and Ayo Dosunmu have carried the perimeter, and the Wolves' 104.1 defensive rating is one of the league's best. New York is 8-6, healthy across the board, and Jalen Brunson has scored 69 points in his last two games. Our fair number makes the Knicks a narrow 51.3% favorite, and no price on the side clears our 0.75% bar. No true edge, but the lean is New York -1.5: the healthy side with the hotter star, against a Wolves team that is thriving without Edwards — so this one is thin. The prop angle is the real edge here: Brunson is over 2.5 threes in 9 of his last 10, averaging 3.6 a game, and Fanatics is hanging +105.
games.title: Knicks at Timberwolves: a coin flip, and Brunson's threes
games.verdict: LEAN: NYK -1.5 — no true edge on the side; the healthy Knicks with Brunson hot, against a Wolves side 8-3 without Edwards.
